title: Morning watch tactical bulletin — first watch handoff
content:
TL;DR:
- Overnight: two related incidents affecting streaming responses for a subset of EU customers (eu-central1). Root cause appears to be transient KV cache invalidations leading to cold-start tokenization regressions and stuck streams.
- Severity: S2 then downgraded once partial mitigation applied; still noisy alerts.
- Current state: primary mitigation in place (force-fallback to model-variant v1.3-compat for active sessions in eu-central1), traffic normalized but metric noise persists.

Summary & timeline (UTC):
- 02:06 — Pager: elevated 5xx rate on /v1/stream for eu-central1 (alerts threshold >0.8% error rate).
- 02:09 — On-call (Leah) acknowledges, opens incident JIRA-INC-2348, posts to #ops-bridge with initial triage.
- 02:14 — Observed spike in cache-miss rate on KV cache tier (cache-frontend-exporter.miss_rate +150% vs baseline).
- 02:22 — First mitigation: route new streaming requests to model-variant v1.3-compat in eu-central1 (lower memory working set) — immediate reduction in error rate.
- 02:35 — Secondary spikes observed: some long-lived client connections reporting stalled frames (streaming keepalive not progressing). Suspected tokenization edge-case after cache purge.
- 03:05 — Applied temporary rate-limiter tweak for long-poll sessions (soft cap 60 reqs/min per client) — reduced stuck-stream reports.
- 04:12 — Alerts down to baseline but cache-miss exporter still noisy. Incident downgraded to S3 and follow-ups assigned (JIRA-INC-2352 for postmortem + runbook updates).

Impact details: 
- Affected surface: streaming generation endpoints only; non-streaming completion and embeddings unaffected. Roughly 6% of EU streaming sessions experienced at least one stall during the 02:00–03:30 window.
- Customer impact: several paying customers reported degraded streaming UX; CS notified and post-incident template queued by Marco.

Root cause hypothesis (work-in-progress):
- Preceding deploy earlier in the day introduced an aggressive prefix-eviction in the KV cache (infra change in autoscale policy + cache purger TTL conflict). When combined with a burst of long-context streaming requests, some worker processes were forced to rehydrate KV state in a path that triggers a rare tokenization failure for certain Unicode sequences, leading to indefinite stream wait states.
- Evidence: correlation between cache purge events in logs and first observed stuck-stream reports; tokenization exceptions logged on ~120 traces (stack snippets attached in JIRA).

Actions taken during shift: 
- Immediate: rollback of the aggressive cache eviction flag in the serving runtime for eu-central1.
- Tactical: automatic fallback routing for new streaming sessions to v1.3-compat model-variant in eu-central1.
- Throttle: soft per-client rate limit applied to long-lived streams to prevent buildup of stalled sessions.
- Communication: pushed to #ops-bridge and paged CS; created JIRA-INC-2348 (active) and JIRA-INC-2352 (follow-ups/postmortem).

Monitoring & metrics checked: 
- grafana/dashboard: streaming-ops/eu-central1/errors, kv-cache/miss-rate, kv-cache/rehydrate-latency, model-runtime/oom-events.
- Traces: sampled traces for 02:00–03:30 to validate tokenization exception patterns.

Outstanding follow-ups (owners + ETA):
- Add precise cache eviction telemetry and trace correlation id in serving-runtime logs — owner: Marco Ruiz — ETA: 2026-08-25.
- Postmortem writeup draft (JIRA-INC-2352) including customer impact notes and RCA writeup — owner: Leah Kim + Anika Shah — ETA: 2026-08-24.
- Runbook update: add a dedicated play for "KV cache mass eviction" including automatic fallback to compatible model variant and explicit cache-warmup steps for active nodes — owner: Corinne Patel — ETA: 2026-08-26.
- Fix: replace the TTL conflict pattern in autoscale/cacher config and add a canary for eviction aggressiveness — owner: infra-config team (assigned in PR #412) — ETA: PR review by 2026-08-23.
- Customer comms: CS to send coordinated note to impacted customers with mitigation summary and SLA impact (Marco) — ETA: 2026-08-23 morning.

Runbook notes / quick edits to make now (for next-run):
- New checklist entry: "If eu streaming error rate > 0.6% & kv-cache miss spike > 100%: route new sessions to model-variant v1.3-compat, disable cache-eviction-flag, and throttle long-lived streams."
- Add a troubleshooting command snippet for quickly forcing a model-variant route for a region (kubectl/traffic-shift snippet).

Things we tried that didn't help:
- Restarting individual workers in eu-central1: helped for single processes but did not affect systemic cache miss pattern.
- Increasing JWT refresh windows: unrelated to observed traces.

Notes to next shift / handoff items: 
- Keep an eye on kv-cache/rehydrate-latency and model-runtime/tokenizer-exception-rate for the next 48h. Any sustained elevation should trigger immediate rollback of the eviction flag and full traffic reroute.
- If the postmortem shows tokenization library bug, we may need to pin the tokenizer dependency across serving images (coord with release-eng).
- Ensure CS has sent customer comms before EOD APAC to avoid duplicate outreach.
- Slack thread summary pinned to incident JIRA (see linked artifacts) — please update with any follow-up notes so the PM and CS teams can see progress.

Questions / decisions needed from on-call handovers: 
- Do we want a temporary automatic warmup job that pre-populates KV for nodes coming out of eviction? (Pros: reduces cold-start faults. Cons: extra RPS during recovery.) Input needed from infra crew.
- Confirm whether traffic routing to v1.3-compat remains acceptable long-term for any high-throughput customers — Ops/Account team feedback required.

Appendix: quick commands and links
- Incident ticket: JIRA-INC-2348 (live) — https://rwd.atl/browse/JIRA-INC-2348
- Postmortem ticket: JIRA-INC-2352 — https://rwd.atl/browse/JIRA-INC-2352
- PR: infra/cache-config change — https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/412
- Grafana dashboard: streaming-ops/eu-central1 — https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streaming-eu

Notes to self (informal):
- There are still a couple of noisy synthetic tests failing in eu-cached suite (synth-stream-07 and -09). Not blocking, but file under flakiness follow-up.
- Remember to capture a handful of failed traces into the postmortem artifact folder (I dumped the first 50 to the incident attachments).

End of first-watch handoff. Next: handover to second-watch at 09:00 UTC — mention the follow-ups above during live bridge.

-- Leah
